novel_mechanics_found: Level 8 contains three same-colored 2x2 tokens and three targets disguised as sets of four tiny 1x1 corner dots. The paired glyphs at right are reversible per-row spacing controls, while the paired glyphs at bottom advance or reverse a shared wrapping conveyor. The row settings synchronize each token's socket-arrival phase: top-left once, middle-right three times, and bottom-right three times make two conveyor advances align all three simultaneously.
narrative: The resolver's 96-click prefix was replayed unchanged and confirmed levels_completed=7 before exploration. Frame-only probing identified the three corner-marked sockets and showed that row shifts alter relative conveyor arrival phases; after an exploratory episode hit the level action limit, a clean episode synchronized the three phases and observed the terminal level-8 win live. The reduced 105-click full line then passed reproduce() from a fresh reset with reached_level=8 and reproduced=true; the winning frame reports state=WIN and win_levels=8, so no further level remains.
gotchas: The action that wins a level immediately renders the next level, so the solved board is not externally visible.
On L8, the three targets are the 2x2 empty regions enclosed by four tiny corner pixels; the larger paired glyphs are controls, not targets.
The right-side left/right halves reversibly shift row spacing, and the bottom left/right halves advance/reverse the global conveyor.
Tokens do not lock when they enter a socket; all three must occupy their sockets on the same conveyor phase.
L8 has a bounded action counter and returns GAME_OVER when exhausted, so cancel exploratory control pairs and replay the reduced configuration on a clean episode.
